What the video changes

A standard 10% loss allowance gives an initial 1.43% of the account per position. On $25k that is $357.14 before lot rounding. On $50k it is $714.29—not $285.71, which assumes only $2k of loss allowance.

Open trades do not shrink the literal closed-balance buffer. Profits can therefore enlarge sizing faster than the daily limit permits.

Most useful comparison

Retain the existing FTMO guard. Its 0.5% initial-capital ceiling already prevents literal ÷7 sizing from expanding normally.

The combined 17-EA roster benefits from a shared cap: 0.5% per trade, 2% open risk, 1% per symbol and a 2% daily admission reserve. This is a tested candidate—not installed.

Costs matter more than the headline

Stress each positive gross trade by −10%, each negative gross trade by +10%, then charge another 0.05R. Under this deliberately adverse execution scenario, the 17-EA portfolios lose much of their challenge-passing edge.

Do not choose the highest modelled return without checking this sensitivity.

Verified rules & operational eligibility

Current rules applied retrospectively to saved history. Programmes have no overall challenge deadline; 180 days is our observation horizon, not a firm deadline. KYC/review time and fees are excluded. Funded profit is retained; withdrawals and payout/fee ROI are not modelled.

Method, limits & audit

Freeze inputs and policies first, replay entries and exits chronologically, size only from cash known at entry, round lots down, then resample whole 28-day Monday-start blocks. Concurrent source signals stay together; original holding durations carry across blocks. Whole-block seams can distort correlations and flat-account eligibility, especially for long-holding bots.
